text:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] p99 streaming latency spike detected on cont-batch path (us-west-2). p95 ~ 420ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~ 1.2s -> 3.4s. Active pages: 2. Paging oncall.

alex (oncall): I see the alert. Confirming impact: streaming requests to model-x-contbatch. Any customer-facing errors?

customer-success: two customers reported degraded response times in dashboards, not 5xxs. They see stalls in streaming and some client-side timeouts.

priya: grabbing traces from jaeger now — looks like a subset of requests hitting large-batch windows where seq-len variance is high. Mixed short/long sequences causing packing stalls.

juan: logs show batcher queue depth spike and a few pack cycles waiting > 1s. snippet: ```
[batcher] pack_cycle=476 wait_ms=1123 packed=18 avg_seq=412 max_seq=2048
[stream] kv_cache_miss=0.04 stall_ms=950
```

alex (oncall): ok this smells like mixed-seqlen amplification + scheduler fairness starvation. We need rapid mitigation to reduce tail. Options: 1) route affected traffic off cont-batch to streaming-only path (lower throughput, lower batching). 2) lower batch_max_size or reduce pack timeout. 3) force preemptive scheduling fairness patch (hotfix).

eng-runtime: canary fallback to non-continuous batching path is ready (flag: enable_stream_fallback). We can flip for one cluster while we tune. Impact: 10-20% higher token cost, lower p99.

alex (oncall): do it. Flip canary on one node pool in us-west-2 and monitor p99. Priya, Juan you take tuning. Carla, coordinate customer comms.

ops-bot: @eng-runtime canary toggle accepted. Running: `redwoodctl feature-toggle set enable_stream_fallback --cluster=usw2-canary --on`

deploy-bot: rollout started for cluster=usw2-canary by eng-runtime. Watch logs: /deploys/usw2/canary/1801239876

priya: while that's rolling, pushing a quick pack timeout reduction on batcher: pack_timeout_ms  -> 30ms from 100ms in the canary config. This reduces wait amplification. Command:
```
kubectl set env deployment/batcher PACK_TIMEOUT_MS=30 -n inference-canary
```

juan: also lowering batch_max_size to 32 for canary: `BATCH_MAX=32`. That should prevent huge packs caused by a few long sequences.

sre-runbook-bot: runbook reminder: if p99 doesn't drop within 2 minutes of fallback, escalate to runtime lead and consider KV eviction of very large contexts.

eng-runtime: canary reports: p99 dropped from 3.4s -> 590ms within 40s of toggle. p95 back to ~300ms. Good signal.

alex (oncall): nice. Can we snapshot metrics and traces for postmortem? Priya take traces for the affected pack cycles.

priya: snapshotting dashboards and exporting top traces. Link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streams/contbatch-usw2?from=now-15m to=now

carla: sending customer update: "We're investigating streaming stalls. We have a mitigation in place (canary fallback) and are monitoring. No data loss. Expecting improved latency within minutes."

customer-success: customers acknowledged, one asks if this will cause reduced throughput — pls advise.

alex (oncall): yes — throughput will be slightly lower on the fallback path; we're prioritizing latency for now. We'll roll to all nodes if stable.

eng-runtime: plan: 1) continue canary for 10m, 2) roll pack_timeout and batch_max_size to remaining nodes, 3) enable preemptive fairness (scheduler) to avoid starvation by large sequences, 4) postmortem and autotune suggestions. I can run steps 1 and 2 now.

juan: also recommend quanta-based preemption: short-seq requests get priority in pack formation for streaming paths. We'll enable a lightweight heuristic on canary to validate.

ops-bot: canary health checks passing. p99=590ms, error rate normal.

alex (oncall): roll to full cluster please, staggered 2 nodes at a time. Use 60s gaps. Signal-wait on p99 regression > 200ms.

eng-runtime: starting staggered rollout. Command (example):
```
redwoodctl rollout batcher --cluster=usw2 --set PACK_TIMEOUT_MS=30,BATCH_MAX=32 --stagger=2 --wait=60
```

priya: tracing shows the worst packs had single requests with seqlen >2000 blocking small ones. Post-rollout we should add a pack-splitting heuristic for very long contexts.

carla: customers updated. No priority escalations.

alex (oncall): assigning owners: eng-runtime (lead rollout) @eng-runtime, tracing + root cause priya, scheduler fairness juan, postmortem carla. I'll update incident channel and close paging once rollout completes and metrics stable for 15m.

eng-runtime: rolled to 8/10 nodes, p99 steady ~600ms. Continuing.

ops-bot: monitor alert cleared for us-west-2 cont-batch p99 spike.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — latency p99 returned to baseline after mitigations and rollout. Please file incident report: tag labels = [cont-batch, mixed-seqlen, p99, canary-fallback].

carla: creating short postmortem and action items: 1) pack-splitting for very long sequences, 2) default batch_max_size lower for mixed-traffic clusters, 3) automatic canary fallback if p99 > threshold, 4) add customer-facing KB.

alex (oncall): thanks team. If anything new pops up, reopen this thread. :thumbsup:

sre-runbook-bot: checklist complete. Closing runbook for this incident."
